question: The hook's stated intent is to inject when the prompt *invokes* deep-research or ultracode. Does its string match separate invocation from mention?

trigger_rates.hook_sha256_note: Historical: the hash of hooks/inject.sh as this run measured it. The file has changed since in comment-only edits (the header's 'invokes' was corrected to 'contains' per claim 1, and the bench paths it cites moved when bench/ was namespaced by plugin); the grep itself is byte-identical and the scorer was re-run after each for the same 4/4 and 8/8. No current-HEAD hash is recorded here deliberately — two of them went stale within a day. bench/validate.py re-runs this scorer on every check, so behaviour drift fails the build instead of a hash quietly rotting.

in_the_wild.note: Eval item 5 is not a designed case. It is the prompt that fired the hook during an unrelated conversation on 2026-08-20 (repository renaming), transcribed byte-for-byte. It is scored by the same verifier as the designed items.

injection_cost.how: stdout of one firing invocation, measured with wc -c; the token figure divides by 4 bytes/token for English prose and is estimated, not tokenized

cross_batch_coverage.note: The same hook run read-only against the frozen 2026-08-06 eval, which was written for the skill description and is unmodified here. Backs claim 4; the two eval sets remain non-comparable as instruments, this is the hook measured on the older set's queries.

notes: Pilot, n=1 per item by design: the apparatus is a shell grep with no model in it, so the measurement is deterministic and has no rate to average. Confirmed by re-running the scorer twice and hashing its JSON output — identical (8f1329a897b3…). The protocol's floor of 3 repetitions per query addresses stochastic trigger rates and does not apply here. No agents ran, so agents[] is empty and every total is zero — this record carries no cost claim about the pipeline; the injection_cost figure is the size of the hook's own payload, and its token count is estimated rather than tokenized. This run does not compare arms and supports no improvement claim; it establishes the current behaviour of hook sha256 ee999cd4… against a newly frozen eval. It is a separate benchmark from 2026-08-06-trigger-eval, which measured the skill *description* under a model judge; the two eval sets are not comparable and neither number transfers to the other mechanism.
